name: onbuy-mcp
description: OnBuy (ecommerce channels): me, update_listing, set_inventory, end_listing, list_orders, mark_shippe

platform_mcp_onbuy_consumer_key.title: PLATFORM_MCP_ONBUY_CONSUMER_KEY
platform_mcp_onbuy_consumer_key.description: Consumer key from the OnBuy/OnCommerce Seller Control Panel > Integrations > OnBuy API (Test and Live keys differ).

platform_mcp_onbuy_secret_key.title: PLATFORM_MCP_ONBUY_SECRET_KEY
platform_mcp_onbuy_secret_key.description: Secret key from the same page; exchanged with the consumer key at POST /v2/auth/request-token for a 15-minute access token (bound to the calling IP), sent as the raw Authorization header.

platform_mcp_onbuy_site_id.title: PLATFORM_MCP_ONBUY_SITE_ID
platform_mcp_onbuy_site_id.description: OnBuy site id your listings/orders belong to: 2000 = OnBuy UK (GET /v2/sites lists the others).

tools.name: me
tools.description: No seller-profile call without the seller id; the probe obtains a token (verifying the consumer/secret keys) and reads the configured site.

tools.name: update_listing
tools.description: Product Listings: Update by SKU — PUT /v2/listings/by-sku {site_id, listings: [{sku, price, stock}]} changes the LIVE price and/or stock of your listing; `listing_id` is your SKU. Per-SKU problems come back in results[].error (e.g. 'SKU does not exist') with HTTP 200 — check raw/error. Title/description belong to the product (OPC) and are not changed here.

tools.name: set_inventory
tools.description: Update by SKU with {sku, stock}: sets the stock of one listing (`sku` required). Per-SKU errors are returned in results[].error with HTTP 200.

tools.name: end_listing
tools.description: Product Listings: Delete by SKU — DELETE /v2/listings/by-sku {site_id, skus: [sku]} DELETES your listing (the product/OPC remains; re-listing needs a new create). `listing_id` is your SKU; the per-SKU outcome ({status: ok} or {error}) is in raw.results.

tools.name: list_orders
tools.description: Orders: Browse — filter[status] awaiting_dispatch (the default when omitted) | dispatched | partially_dispatched | cancelled | cancelled_by_seller | cancelled_by_buyer | refunded | partially_refunded | all; since = filter[date_from] as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. price_total is a decimal string; buyer, addresses and products are in raw. No page parameters are documented, so only the first result page is returned.

tools.name: mark_shipped
tools.description: Orders: Dispatch — PUT /v2/orders/dispatch {site_id, orders: [{order_id, tracking: {supplier_name, number}}]} marks the WHOLE order dispatched and e-mails the buyer. supplier_name (`carrier`) is required whenever a tracking number is sent and is for internal reference only (OnBuy detects the courier from the number). Per-order success/failure is in raw.results[order_id].
